articles.title: What is a HAR file, and how to get one from Chrome
articles.excerpt: A HAR file (HTTP Archive) is a JSON file that records every network request a browser made while a page was open, including URLs, headers, request bodies, responses and timings. Support teams ask for…
articles.body: A HAR file (HTTP Archive) is a JSON file that records every network request a browser made while a page was open, including URLs, headers, request bodies, responses and timings. Support teams ask for one because it shows exactly what your browser sent and received when something broke. You can generate a HAR file in Chrome from the Network panel in DevTools in under a minute. Disclosure: I build Netraptor , which this guide mentions as one option. The steps work with plain Chrome and free tools. Steps Open the Network panel. Go to the page with the problem and open DevTools with F12, Ctrl+Shift+I on Windows and Linux, or Cmd+Option+I on macOS. Click the Network tab. Turn on Preserve log. Check Preserve log so requests are kept across page loads and redirects.
articles.author: Parth V Square

articles.title: What is an OpenAPI spec, and how to generate one from your web app's traffic
articles.excerpt: An OpenAPI spec is a JSON or YAML document that describes an HTTP API in a standard, language-agnostic format, listing its paths, methods, parameters, request bodies and responses. If your API has no…
articles.body: An OpenAPI spec is a JSON or YAML document that describes an HTTP API in a standard, language-agnostic format, listing its paths, methods, parameters, request bodies and responses. If your API has no spec yet, you can generate a first draft from real traffic by recording the requests your web app makes in Chrome, exporting them as a HAR file, and converting that file with an open-source tool such as mitmproxy2swagger. You then review the draft by hand, because traffic only shows what was actually called. Disclosure: I build Netraptor , which this guide mentions as one option. The steps work with plain Chrome and free tools. Steps Record the app's API calls in Chrome.

articles.title: Next.js Security Update October 2026: Patch the use cache RCE, SVG sharp RCE and Server Actions DoS

articles.body: The Next.js security update of October 14, 2026 fixes three vulnerabilities: two critical unauthenticated remote code execution (RCE) bugs, one in use cache and one in SVG image optimization through sharp , and a high severity denial of service in Server Actions. Upgrade to Next.js 16.4.1 or later on 16.x, or 15.5.28 on 15.x, make sure sharp is 0.35.5 or later , then rebuild and redeploy. The patch is easy to apply and easy to get wrong when you self-host. I reproduced the upgrade on real installs and found that upgrading Next.js 15 to 15.5.28 left the vulnerable sharp 0.34.5 in place , while npm audit on an unpatched next@16.4.0 reported 0 vulnerabilities .

articles.title: Deterministic linters for AI-written technical prose (EN, RU, ES, DE, FR)
articles.excerpt: Most "AI slop" advice is a style guide. This is a checker. The symptom: documentation that reads fine in review and breaks the reader later. A sentence that hides the actor. A run-on that buries the c…
articles.body: Most "AI slop" advice is a style guide. This is a checker. The symptom: documentation that reads fine in review and breaks the reader later. A sentence that hides the actor. A run-on that buries the command. A paragraph of hedges. Nobody flags it during review, because review is where prose gets read politely. It surfaces in the incident, in the support ticket, in the runbook nobody can follow at 3 a.m. Anti-slop-kit has two halves. A skill tells the model how to write. A linter proves whether the model did it. The linter is the half most advice leaves out, because rules are easy to state and annoying to enforce.
articles.author: ameobius

articles.body: Someone buys a chapter in your Android app. It opens, and they start reading. From the app screen, the purchase looks finished. There is one more result to check: did Google Play receive confirmation that your app processed it? The 30-second illustration shows those two outcomes side by side. It is an example flow, not a recording of a customer purchase. What can go wrong For a completed purchase, your app needs to verify the purchase, grant the right access, and tell Play it was processed. If an eligible purchase is left unacknowledged, Play can automatically refund it and revoke the entitlement. A consumable follows a different final step: consuming it also fulfills the acknowledgment requirement.

articles.excerpt: Teams at NASA’s Stennis Space Center near Bay St. Louis, Mississippi tested RS-25 engine No. 10001 on Oct. 21, 2026. The hot fire test lasted for almost eight-and-a-half minutes (500 seconds), the sam…
articles.body: NASA/Danny Nowlin Teams at NASA’s Stennis Space Center near Bay St. Louis, Mississippi tested RS-25 engine No. 10001 on Oct. 21, 2026. The hot fire test lasted for almost eight-and-a-half minutes (500 seconds), the same amount of time RS-25 engines fire during launch of NASA’s SLS (Space Launch System) rocket, with a 111% power level. For each Artemis mission, four RS-25 engines produce up to 2 million pounds of combined thrust to help launch the SLS rocket. Prior to use, all RS-25 engines are proven flightworthy at NASA Stennis. While this developmental engine will not be used in flight, the hot fire test provides NASA and NASA’s prime engine contractor L3Harris Technologies with the capability to capture critical data to improve engine performance and reliability.

articles.excerpt: This incredible composite image of Orionid meteors was captured as Earth passed through the debris trail shed by Halley's Comet.
articles.body: Tim McCollum captured a stunning view of Orionid meteors in the early hours of Oct. 21. (Image credit: Tim McCollum) Astrophotographer Tim McCollum captured a spectacular view of Orionid meteors sharing the night sky with a host of deep sky wonders on Oct. 21, as the annual shooting star display ramped up to peak activity. Comet 1P/Halley may be over 3 billion miles (4.8 kilometers) from Earth , but that didn't stop it from putting on a breathtaking display earlier this week, as particles cast off by the ancient wanderer carved a fiery path through the autumn sky. McCollum was able to capture a trio of vivid Orionid meteors as they streaked through the night sky above the city of Toccoa, Georgia, between 3-4 a.m. on Oct. 21.

articles.title: Never finishing the fight: Where did Xbox go wrong with Halo?
articles.excerpt: After a failed soft reboot and a remake of the original, the Halo universe is facing yet another major creative shift. But has Xbox learned any lessons this time?
articles.body: Halo: Campaign Evolved was Xbox’s second attempt at refreshing the 2001 sci-fi FPS classic, and it is perfectly fine. A cromulent remake, if ever there was one, but it’s hardly a franchise-saver, especially as Xbox looks to rethink its studio structure and approach to renowned IPs like Halo or Gears of War . Halo hasn’t been the same since original developer Bungie — now owned by Sony and working on Destiny and Marathon — departed, leaving 343 Industries (now Halo Studios) to guide the franchise. Neither Halo 4 nor 5 meaningfully evolved the gameplay formula or overarching narrative. Halo Infinite found more success by reheating what “old Halo felt like” and sticking it into a half-baked open world, but it still felt far from the series’ glory days.

articles.title: Private Griffin moon lander gets put to the test | Space photo of the day for Oct. 23, 2026
articles.excerpt: The robotic Griffin lunar lander has passed a host of critical tests ahead of its first-ever moon mission, which is scheduled to launch later this year.
articles.body: The Griffin-1 lunar lander undergoes testing at NASA's Jet Propulsion Lab. (Image credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech) The robotic Griffin lunar lander has passed a host of critical tests ahead of its first-ever moon mission, which is scheduled to launch later this year. What is it? At NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) in Southern California, Voyager Technologies' Griffin Mission One (or Griffin-1 ) lunar lander has gone through an absolute gauntlet of tests. The spacecraft was put through environmental testing that explored how the vehicle will fare in the extreme conditions it will experience on its ride to the surface of the moon . This testing simulated the extreme temperatures, shaking and even the sounds that the spacecraft will experience from launch to landing.
